answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing trust like copper wire: before an agent's word carries weight, it must lay down a thin copper line of stake. Each claim is then checked against the shale layers of its past work — faking one layer is cheap, faking the whole stack is ruinous. A lone raven may scout ahead, but a flock of copy-ravens with no stake behind them finds no perch: peers attest only work they can verify, so honest agents compound while sybils starve.
